thread:
Cheng Li: heads-up — EU-west spot pools are showing sustained shortages this morning, eviction spikes across p3* shapes. considering a hedged approach: small on-demand hot-standby, shorter spot leases, and a lightweight request requeue queue. thoughts?
Alex Kim: yikes, saw the metric. is this across multiple AZs or concentrated?
Cheng Li: mostly az-1 and az-2. az-3 still OK but capacity fragmentation means our packing drops. overall spot capacity index down ~40% for GPUs.
Maria Gonzalez: partial idea — keep a tiny on-demand pool per-region (~5% of baseline) that we only spin up when preempt rate crosses threshold. cheaper than constantly overprovisioning.
Samir Patel: +1. also we should prioritize graceful handoff for in-flight streaming sessions. if we cut a node, the runtime should publish a short-lived replay token to S3/redis and mark request for requeue.
Cheng Li: exactly. current problem is token continuity when switching from spot->on-demand. our streaming token broker assumes sticky session. we need a cutover that doesn't force full replay for short prompts.
Alex Kim: can we augment the autoscaler to do predictive hedging? e.g., if market volatility > X then pre-emptively maintain hot-standby until volatility subsides.
Maria Gonzalez: yes, and combine with backoff windows: new long-running sessions prefer on-demand; short burst inference still go to spot. split by max-seq-length or estimated duration.
Samir Patel: operationally we should add a tiny FIFO retry queue with TTL 30s to hold requests during cutover. runtime would: 1) attempt streaming token bridge 2) if fail -> enqueue request id -> return minimal progress token to client -> worker on hotpool picks it up and resumes.
Cheng Li: sketch of autoscaler policy snippet:
```yaml
scale_policy:
  region: eu-west-1
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    volatility_threshold: 0.3   # preempt rate fraction
    hot_standby_ratio: 0.05
    standby_min_count: 2
    cooldown_s: 120
```
Alex Kim: looks good. we should also track cost delta (hot-standby runtime cost) vs SLO misses. need dashboard metric: "eviction_cost_saved" and "hot_standby_cost".
Maria Gonzalez: runtime changes: token bridge proto must support a resume token that includes KV-cache pointers and model-version hash. can pack as base64 small envelope. something like: `resume_v1:{model}:{kv_ptr}:{nonce}`.
Samir Patel: add operational play: when eviction event arrives -> node marks draining -> runtime publishes `drain:node_id:epoch` event -> workers start 5s graceful flush -> streaming sessions get `resume_token` via header x-resume-token. fallback path uses FIFO queue.
ops-bot: incident: preemptible-evict-alert eu-west-1 at 1761237000 (auto-notify, severity low)
Cheng Li: thanks, ops-bot. action items: 1) Alex to prototype autoscaler hedging hook, 2) Maria to add resume-token header + FIFO enqueue path, 3) Samir to add dashboard panels + SLO delta calc. target: small experiment by EOD tomorrow.
Alex Kim: I'll stub the hedging controller and a k8s CRD for standby pools.
Maria Gonzalez: I'll add header and minimal resume token envelope to runtime. will reuse redis for short TTL queue.
Samir Patel: I'll wire up the dashboard and a simple cost/SLO simulation script.
Cheng Li: cool. let's keep the requeue logic minimal first — prefer resume over full replay. we can iterate once we see metrics.
Alex Kim: one more note — network egress patterns during hot-standby spinups might trigger rate limits from cloud vendor. add jitter and soft-start.
Maria Gonzalez: noted. will add exponential jitter on instance creation (base 2s).
Samir Patel: if we hit provider rate limits frequently, fallback to cross-region spill to az-3. keep that as last resort.
Cheng Li: great. thanks everyone. ping @channel with updates.
